deep.reconstruction:
Folio 15 has no mathematical derivation. It has two parts.

(A) A reading or acquisition list of travel and geography books, apparently around 1818–1821. The next page is headed 'Neue Bücher von 1821'. The entries are:
- P. S. Pallas, Bemerkungen auf einer Reise in die südlichen Statthalterschaften des Russischen Reichs (1799–1801), Th. 1–2.
- E. D. Clarke, Travels in various countries of Europe, Asia and Africa, vols. 1–5.
- J. von Hammer, Topographische Ansichten gesammelt auf einer Reise in die Levante (Wien 1811).
- A. von Humboldt, Voyage … Relation historique, tome 1 ff.
- Lady Craven, journey to the Crimea. Gauss wrote 'Reise' and struck it out.
- M. v. Engelhardt & F. Parrot, Reise in die Krym und den Kaukasus, 2 Theile (1815).
- A. von Humboldt, Ansichten der Natur, Theil 1–2.
- Voyage de découvertes aux terres australes, rédigé par M. F. Péron, T. 1 ff.
- F. Arends, Ostfriesland und Jever in geographischer, statistischer und landwirthschaftlicher Rücksicht, 2 Bde (Emden 1818).
- C. Ritter, Erdkunde.
- L. von Buch, Reise durch Norwegen und Lappland.

(B) A personal measurement: 'Peripherie meiner Hüte unten aussen gemessen', i.e. the circumference of his hats, measured on the outside at the bottom.
- Hat I: C = 902 mm, which he expresses as 1½ Elle + 1/22 (Elle), with the marginal note '1 Zoll'.
- Hat II: C = 891 mm, 'ist etwas zu knapp' (is a bit too tight), expressed as 1½ Elle + 1/39 (Elle).

My reconstruction of the conversion takes the Hannover Elle = 2 Calenberg Fuß = 584.2 mm, with 1 Zoll = 24.34 mm.
- 1½ Elle = 876.3 mm.
- Hat I: excess = 902 − 876.3 = 25.7 mm. This is 0.0440 Elle ≈ 1/22.7 Elle, written as 1/22. It is also about 1.06 Zoll, hence the note '1 Zoll'. Note that 1/22 Elle = 12/11 Zoll ≈ 1.09 Zoll.
- Hat II: excess = 891 − 876.3 = 14.7 mm ≈ 0.0252 Elle ≈ 1/39.7 Elle, written as 1/39.
- Working backwards, Gauss's fractions imply an Elle of 902/(3/2 + 1/22) ≈ 583.6 mm and 891/(3/2 + 1/39) ≈ 584.0 mm. Both agree with the Hannover Elle to within about 0.1%.

This is everyday unit conversion of the same kind as the paper-dimension notes on the previous page.
errors: No real errors. The fractions are rounded approximations.
With Elle = 584.2 mm, the exact excesses are 1/22.7 and 1/39.7 Elle. So 1/23 and 1/40 would be marginally closer than Gauss's 1/22 and 1/39.
Gauss's values are consistent with an Elle of about 583.6–584.0 mm, well within the precision of measuring a hat.

results.what: Conversion of hat circumferences from millimetres to Hannover Elle plus a fraction of an Elle (and Zoll)
Bibliographic list of travel and geographical literature

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a personal book list and a hat-size measurement with a trivial conversion to Hannover units. It has no mathematical content. It is of minor biographical interest only, for Gauss's reading in travel literature and his habit of measuring everyday objects.

checkable.asserts: 1½ Hannover Elle + 1/22 Elle (Elle = 584.2 mm) ≈ 902 mm, within 2 mm
Elle length implied by hat I: about 583.6 mm
Elle length implied by hat II: about 584.0 mm
Excess of hat I over 1½ Elle is about 1.06 Hannover Zoll, matching the marginal '1 Zoll'

transcription_corrections: 'Engelhardt [?] Parrot' should read 'Engelhardt u. Parrot': Moritz von Engelhardt and Friedrich Parrot, Reise in die Krym und den Kaukasus, 1815.
'red. par' is 'réd. par' (rédigé par) M. F. Péron.
'{+unten+}' is a superscript insertion above 'aussen'. The phrase reads 'unten aussen gemessen' (measured at the bottom, outside).
'1 Zoll' at the far right belongs to line I as a marginal equivalent of the excess over 1½ Elle.
In 'Hammer … gesammelt auf einer Reise nach der Levante', the published title reads 'in die Levante'. The manuscript appears to say 'nach der Levante', so this is acceptable as written.
